column3: The Hebrew ends with living on the ground, distinct from the earlier reference to observing the statutes in the land.

The Hebrew says not to do so to the LORD, without an explicit verb for worship.
The Hebrew distinguishes putting His Name there from seeking His dwelling and changes to singular address for going there.
The Hebrew retains the image of the raised offering of your hand.
The Hebrew describes all you do as the putting forth of your hand and changes to singular address in the final blessing clause.
